title: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Dec 2026 data) — 9:30 a.m. CT / 10:30 ET, the only scheduled US data release that lands ON the 2Y/5Y auction Monday
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tmos), fetched direct 2026-09-09 with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200, 42,245 bytes) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup rather than through a summarizing fetcher. The table headed `2026 release dates` carries the column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `December | Monday, December 28`, alongside the note that `The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT. While we strive to ensure the information is published to our website in a timely manner, we cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online.` The same table's `September | Monday, September 28` and `November | Monday, November 30` rows are the ones this calendar's existing dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 and dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 entries were filed against, so the December row is the same series read from the same primary. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (no `FED:` prefix covers a District survey page as opposed to a Board release), and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-09 by the treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28 never-assessed initial research, and it is the D-0 gap that changes how that auction can be read. WHY IT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE: this calendar already carries dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 and dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 from the identical primary, and the sibling Texas Service Sector survey as dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01 — December's manufacturing release is the missing member of an established monthly series, and it is the only one inside this corridor that lands on the auction session itself. WHY IT EARNS A ROW BEYOND SERIES COMPLETENESS: the proposing research's third finding is that 2026-12-28 is NOT an attributable auction day, unlike its 2026-11-23 sibling which carried zero other tracked events. This survey at 10:30 ET is one of the reasons — it sits between the 8:30 advance economic indicators and the 11:30 bill auctions, ahead of the 1:00pm 2Y and 5Y. A tracked entry is what lets the next window-arithmetic pass see the crowding instead of inferring a clean tape. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, `low` impact, the date is `estimate`.
